Standardize a raw dataset with a DGF's rules

stabilize_data.Rd

Applies a DGF's per-variable rules to a raw dataset: first the `desired_data_import_rule` (read the column correctly), then the `raw_to_stable_transform` (standardize it). The result is the "stable" version of the data - what a downstream program should consume.

Usage

stabilize_data(raw, dgf, env = parent.frame(), use_v7 = FALSE)

Arguments

raw

A data frame, or a path to a raw `.csv`.

dgf

A DGF data frame, or a path to a DGF `.xlsx` (read with [load_dgf()]).

env

Environment in which to find the rule functions named in the DGF (e.g. project `dgf.R` helpers). Defaults to the caller's environment.

use_v7

Logical; execute the v7 `stabilizer` plan (the `read :: [convert] :: write` path from formex's transform-path search) for columns that carry no legacy rule. Defaults to `FALSE`, so the legacy behaviour is unchanged. When `TRUE`, a column whose `raw_to_stable_transform` and `desired_data_import_rule` are both blank is transformed by its v7 plan (via [formex::fx_apply_plan()]) when that plan is executable; a legacy rule, where present, always takes precedence, and an identity or unreachable plan leaves the column unchanged. Honours confirm-then-transform: the suggested stabilizer runs only when the caller opts in.

Value

A data frame: the columns the DGF describes, in DGF order, with each rule applied. Columns present in `raw` but absent from the DGF are dropped; a DGF variable with no matching raw column is skipped with a warning.

Details

Legacy rules name a function reachable in `env` and are applied element-wise; a blank rule is a pass-through. This is the same dispatch [create_dgf()] uses, so the built-in helpers ([read_ein()], [read_mm()], ...) and any user function work identically here. With `use_v7 = TRUE`, a rule-free column is instead handed to its v7 stabilizer plan, which is vectorised and type-preserving (it does not stringify through a per-value `as.character`).

See also

[write_stable_csv()], [create_dgf()], [stabilize_col_v7()]
